subject: Importance sampling based LOOCV on multi-type (marked) LGCP

messages.author: ef409dbd3be2e2c7
messages.subject: Importance sampling based LOOCV on multi-type (marked) LGCP
parts:
Dear INLA community,


Hi, I am extending my research to multi-type LGCP from previous question:

https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/r-inla-discussion-group/tyC4CK1pvQc


There are over 200 point sets, marked as type A or type B.

I want to predict where each point set belongs based on loocv.


However, it would be infeasible to perform exact loocv since each estimation process takes ~ 4hours.

Point sets can be grouped by different sources (in the same space), but still we have to perform ~80 estimations.


Hopefully, a Bayesian Point Process Classifier has been proposed by Kang et al. (2014), which is based on importance sampling approach of loocv:

https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.1670

The probability that point set i belongs to type j (T_i = j) is given as

where p_j is prior probability of being type j and it is considered being equal for all types.



Therefore, we are basically classifying point set i by Q_hat, which is given as 

where k = 1, …, K refers to K posterior simulations, and t_i refers to true type of point set i.



The problem is that I have approximated posteriors, while Kang et al. (2014) acquired samples form MCMC.

Is it a comparable approach to sample from approximate posteriors?

Another approach would be just use posterior mode \hat{\theta}.


In this regard, I approached both ways, and there are huge discrepancies between the two likelihoods.

  1. \pi(x_i | T_i = j, \hat{\theta})
  2. 1/K * \sum_{k=1}^K \pi(x_i | T_i = j, \theta^(K))


where simplified \lambda_j = exp(intercept + f(s, model = spde)).


When I plug in likelihood 1 to the classifier, I get somewhat biased, but reasonable overall prediction accuracy ~77%, while the classifier only sticks to type A all the time, when I plugin the likelihood 2.


It seems like the discrepancy comes from few extreme samples of the posterior samples.


In short,

  1. Is it okay to use posterior samples from INLA instead of MCMC? or stick to posterior mode?
  2. How can I deal with the discrepancy between likelihood conditional on posterior mode and expected likelihood from posterior samples?


It seems like Vehtari et al. (2014) have dealt with similar problems:

https://arxiv.org/abs/1412.7461

which seems to be implemented in the “loo” package, 

but I have no idea whether it would be possible to apply it into my problem:

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/loo/vignettes/loo2-large-data.html

maybe you can use the marginal likelihood. the posterior.samples from
inla.posterior.samples are pretty accurate. maybe using the marginal
likelihood estimate result$mlik can be useful as well.
